The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command sources the PKGBUILD in a restricted context, executing only top-level code and not running any of the package functions (`pkgver`, `prepare`, `build`, `package`). In this PKGBUILD, the top-level consists solely of standard variable assignments (e.g., `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `source`, `sha256sums`) with no command substitutions, function calls, or executable statements outside of function definitions.

Notably, the `source` array references a git repository from the declared upstream (`https://github.com/xiaoqidun/ofdgo`), and while the checksum is set to 'SKIP', this is expected and normal for VCS-based packages and does not pose a risk during `--printsrcinfo` since no download or verification occurs at this stage. There are no top-level shell expansions, `$(...)` substitutions, or `eval` calls that could trigger arbitrary code execution when sourcing the file.

Thus, merely sourcing this PKGBUILD for metadata extraction poses no security risk.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It declares standard package information such as name, description, dependencies, source location, and checksums. The source is set to a Git repository at `https://github.com/xiaoqidun/ofdgo.git`, which matches the package's declared upstream URL. This is a normal practice for `-git` packages in the AUR.

The `sha256sums = SKIP` entry is expected and appropriate for VCS (Git) sources, as the content is not a fixed tarball but a mutable repository. AUR tools like `makepkg` handle this safely by relying on the integrity of the Git clone operation. There are no network operations, script executions, or file manipulations defined in this file — it is purely declarative metadata.

No malicious or suspicious behavior is present. The package depends only on standard build tools (go, git) and runtime libraries (glibc, hicolor-icon-theme), which are reasonable for a Go application with GUI components. The `options = !debug` disables debug symbols, a common optimization. Overall, this file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and poses no security risk.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Standard AUR metadata, no malicious content</summary>
</security_assessment>

The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is normal for VCS sources and not inherently unsafe, as checksums cannot be determined in advance for mutable git repositories.

The build process uses standard Go tooling with secure build flags such as `-trimpath`, `-buildmode=pie`, and `-mod=readonly`. No network operations, file downloads, or external code execution occur during prepare, build, or package phases. All installed files (binary, icon, license, desktop entry) are sourced directly from the cloned repository and installed to standard system directories. The desktop entry is generated inline with static, safe content.

There are no signs of obfuscated code, unexpected file operations, data exfiltration, or execution of untrusted code. The operations are consistent with legitimate packaging practices for a Go application. While the source uses an unpinned git reference (common for -git packages), this is not malicious by itself.
</details>
